name: Heinfels
kurzbeschreibung: Charming market town in the Pustertal with the eponymous Burg Heinfels – the iconic landmark of Tiroler Pustertal.
beschreibung:
Overview

Heinfels is situated at an elevation of 1,078 metres in the Upper Pustertal valley in East Tyrol, within the district of Lienz, right at the confluence of the Tyrolean Gailtal and the Pustertal. The municipality spans roughly 15 square kilometres and is home to around 1,000 residents. Flanked by the dramatic ridges of the Villgraten Mountains and the nearby Lienz Dolomites, Heinfels forms a scenic border gem near South Tyrol. The contemporary municipality was formed in 1974 through the union of the historic villages of Panzendorf and Tessenberg, adopting the name of the majestic fortress that crowns the valley. Heinfels harmoniously combines medieval architecture, authentic alpine traditions, and culinary attractions.

History

Human settlement on the valley floor stretches back to the Middle Ages: Tessenberg was first recorded in 1266 as Tessenperch, while Panzendorf was documented in 1364 as Ponzendorf. The landscape is dominated by glorious Heinfels Castle, affectionately dubbed the Queen of the Pustertal. First recorded around 1240 in records of the Prince-Bishops of Brixen, the castle served as a fortified stronghold for the Counts of Gorizia and as the administrative seat of the court of Heinfels. After centuries of turmoil and neglect, extensive restoration culminated in 2020 with the reopening of the castle as a museum and dining venue. Another engineering landmark is the Punbrugge, erected in 1781, celebrated as Tyrol's longest covered historic wooden bridge.

Getting There

By automobile from the north, take the Felbertauern Road via Lienz, then follow the federal highway B100 westward up through the Pustertal directly to Heinfels. From Innsbruck and the west, drive through South Tyrol via the Puster Valley Road SS49 past San Candido (Innichen) across the Austrian border. Train travellers ride the scenic Pustertal Railway: ÖBB and South Tyrol regional trains stop at neighbouring Sillian station or Heinfels/Tassenbach. The station is seamlessly connected to VVT regional buses. Cyclists can pedal directly into the village along the famous international Drau Cycle Path.

Tips

Exploring Heinfels Castle is an absolute must: Guided tours lead through historic courtyards, subterranean dungeons, and up the keep for panoramic vistas across the valley. Down along the river, the wooden Punbrugge bridge provides an iconic photo backdrop. Families and sweet lovers should visit the Loacker World of Goodness (Loacker Genusswelt), where interactive exhibits and a pastry workshop allow guests to create bespoke wafer treats. Outdoor enthusiasts will enjoy cycling the gentle Drau Cycle Path towards Lienz or embarking on panoramic hikes to Tessenberg and the tranquil Villgraten peaks.
